Seats: Wikipedia infobox, cross-checked against Politpro.eu, IPU Parline and Parikiaki news coverage of the 24 May 2026 result. Government support status: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christodoulides_government and https://whogoverns.eu/cyprus-2026-stability-at-the-top-revolt-at-the-bottom/ (both confirm DIKO as sole remaining formal coalition/support partner after EDEK and DIPA lost their seats).

note: Held 24 May 2026, well before this dataset's 2026-09-14 cutoff; results certified (66.91% turnout, DISY retained its lead). Cyprus has a presidential system: the President (Christodoulides, elected 2023, term to 2028) appoints the Council of Ministers independently of the legislature's party composition. Corrected vs. prior version: the Wikipedia article 'Christodoulides government' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christodoulides_government), corroborated by Who Governs Europe's post-election analysis (whogoverns.eu, 'Cyprus 2026: stability at the top, revolt at the bottom'), states Christodoulides entered office in 2023 backed by DIKO, EDEK and DIPA; after the May 2026 election EDEK and DIPA both lost all their seats (fell below the ~3.6% effective threshold), leaving DIKO (8 seats) as the sole party formally still supporting/in the coalition - explicitly described as 'a minority government supported solely by DIKO'. DIKO is therefore marked in_government=true, mirroring the same logic used in Cyprus_2021.json (where ParlGov's post-election cabinet record determined which party, if any, held formal government-support status). No other party (including DISY, whose leader is not part of the formal coalition despite some DISY-affiliated figures receiving ministerial posts in an Aug 2026 reshuffle per Cyprus Mail, 2026-08-04, 'President announces partial cabinet reshuffle') is confirmed as formally 'in government'.
